findings.location: scripts/native_qualification_v4.py check_record (entrypoint-label block, lines 394-409, and the backend label block, lines 442-448); README 'Evidence classes' P-b and 'T04 proofs' T04-ENTRYPOINT-CENSUS row
findings.finding: Nothing stops a second enrolled file from carrying a LABEL_BOUND role's (or an ENTRY_BOUND backend's) entrypoint type, or the interpreter type, so a record that itself declares a second entry file for the domain still qualifies. P-b and T04-ENTRYPOINT-CENSUS cover only files outside the enrolled set. The model checks only the subject's own executable label and the exec-segment files of interpreted closures, so the inside-the-set half falls between them. T04-LABELS would then confirm the bad labels as declared. The observer measures only the role's executable, so under P-a the broker, worker or low-port server domain may have been entered through the other file, and 'domain entry plus the measured file' no longer binds the image (backends likewise). Reviewer probes, each with every capture rebound to the mutated record (digest, file observations, the gate's maps): check_record and check_qualification both return None (accepted) for (a) a gate library labelled planeon_broker_exec_t, (b) a worker data file (no executable segment) labelled planeon_worker_exec_t, (c) a server data file labelled planeon_worker_exec_t, (d) a HOST_CONTAINMENT closure library labelled planeon_broker_exec_t, (e) a kubelet library labelled planeon_broker_exec_t, (f) a kubelet library labelled qualk8s_scheduler_exec_t (a second scheduler entry file), and (g) a gate library labelled planeon_interpreter_exec_t, outside every interpreted closure, which the interpreted domains may EXECUTE and so map without the closure recording it.
findings.requiredChange: Add a check_record rule over files and backendFiles: a file whose label is any subject's entrypoint constant (the five roles' and two lifecycle subjects' executableLabel, the eight backend executableLabel constants) must be that subject's executable. planeon_interpreter_exec_t (interpreterLabel) may label only executable-segment files of an interpreted role's closure, never a role, lifecycle or backend executable or a file in a native, lifecycle or backend closure. Optionally also refuse matrix v5's other ENTRYPOINT types (planeon_maint_exec_t, qualk8s_container_file_t) on enrolled files. Add negatives for cases (a)-(g), with the I06 v3 SC00 consequence if any. State in the README (P-b, T04-ENTRYPOINT-CENSUS, Entrypoints and labels) that the in-set half of the census is the model's rule and the out-of-set half is T04's.

findings.location: scripts/native_qualification_v4.py _member_sets (lines 460-473); schema $defs/memberSet (no uniqueness of (pid, startTicks) rows)
findings.finding: The bracket rule does not check that the before/after member sets cover the reported members. _member_sets compares len(before) == len(counts) == len(members) and maps each before row to a member's thread count. It never requires the (pid, startTicks) keys of the rows to be distinct or to equal the members' keys, and the schema has no outer uniqueness. A WORKER capture whose memberSetBefore and memberSetAfter both list the inspected worker twice, omitting co-member 3013, passes check_capture and check_qualification (reviewer probe on positive 1: both None). So a co-member can be reported in cgroupMembers without the frozen-bracket reads showing it before and after. That is the broker-side change inside the bracket which owner decision Q-NP4D-10 (a) and D2-1 require to be refused. The README claim that 'the sets must also be exactly the reported members and thread counts' is not enforced. (Single-process leaves are safe, because len(members) == 1 forces the one row to be the inspected process.)
findings.requiredChange: In _member_sets, require the (pid, startTicks) keys of memberSetBefore to be unique and equal as a set to the members' keys (equality with memberSetAfter then follows from the existing canonical comparison), or make the schema refuse duplicate (pid, startTicks) rows. Add WORKER negatives: duplicate rows hiding a co-member, and one pid listed twice with different thread lists.

findings.location: architecture/native-profile-v4/vectors.json N18-N31, N37-N38; README 'Capture shapes and the proof list' last bullet
findings.finding: Design §3.7 (from D1-5's required change) asks for each forbidden field present 'with an equal and with a different value', and the README claims this coverage. Classifying the vectors against the positives shows a different value only for process.exe (N19 for the low-port server, N24 for the broker, V08 for the observer). executableMaps, namespaceInodes and cgroupMembers[].exe appear only with the observed or recorded value (N20-N23, N25-N31, N37, N38). WORKER has no different-value case at all, and the observer has no equal-value process.exe case and no cgroupMembers[].exe case. Every refusal is presence-based (schema 'not', model membership test), so behaviour is unaffected; this is coverage and a README overclaim.
findings.requiredChange: Add the missing different-value negatives (maps, namespaces and member exe for the broker, the worker and the low-port server; observer member exe and equal-value exe), or narrow the README sentence to what the vectors pin.

findings.finding: By the reviewer's recollection, not verified (no network, no kernel source read), the SELinux user_namespace class and its create permission arrived with the LSM userns_create hook in Linux 6.1, not 6.0. The other versions (Seccomp_filters 5.9, cgroup v2 freezer 5.2, pidfd_open 5.3, CLONE_INTO_CGROUP 5.7, FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY 5.4, BPF_LSM_CGROUP 6.0) match the reviewer's recollection. No effect on the enrolled v6.12 kernel.
findings.requiredChange: Re-check the user_namespace entry, or keep it explicitly as an author's reading for T04 to confirm, as the README already frames it.

findings.finding: The moved text reads 'v2 is also bound to W02a v4 itself'. The sentence describes the model's own binding, so it should name v3. I06 v2 stays bound to W02a v3.
findings.requiredChange: Change that 'v2' to 'v3', or keep v2's sentence and add a v3 one.

findings.finding: v5 supersedes the adopted but unmerged edge v4 by digest (e30772ff..., which equals the file in the amend2 contract directory), and README-v5 requires slot 244 to merge first. If v4's bytes change before or at its merge, v5's supersedes digest and its copy of v4's 45 rows become stale. Neither text says the mechanics re-derive them.

flaggedPoints.reason: criteria.json is the effective v2 criteria byte-for-byte except schemaVersion /v3, SC00 and SC08 requirement texts (v3->v4, SC08 restating that v4 refuses a shared executable but allows shared content) and two source strings; evidence record version /v2 is kept and a v2-format evidence naming another W02a version is refused (X07).

executableLabel/interpreterLabel are schema consts per role, lifecycle subject and backend component; the model compares the executable file row's label with them. All 15 constants and the interpreter type equal matrix v5's unique ENTRYPOINT type per subject (reviewer cross-check). See N1-1 for the missing in-inventory uniqueness.

observerProcess holds only cgroup inode and limits (path is a process-level /proc fact, DECLARED for the observer); observerMember holds only the pid; the model checks exactly one member, inode/limits equality, pidsCurrent <= pidsMax, programs and census, consistent with design §3.3 row 3 and D2-6/D3-6.

Fields and placement are sound (WORKER requires both frozen flags, other roles forbid them, check_capture refuses an unfrozen worker capture so check_qualification fails closed per Q-NP4D-10 (a)), but the member-set coverage rule must require unique keys equal to the members' keys (N1-2).

The seal marker label is DECLARED_T04 (T04-LABELS) in design §3.3; observedHardening.sealMarker drops it and the rest of hardeningObserved keeps v3's equality (reviewer probe: a label in hardeningObserved is refused by the schema).

Backend one-file-per-component by path matches design §3.4 with content distinctness left to SC08 (G19/G20 replay as stated). The ordered t04Proofs const is stricter than 'equal the closed set' but canonical and stated as ordered (a reordered list is refused, reviewer variant). The two messages split 'all OBSERVED fields absent' from 'some absent', both refusals. evidenceClasses is unreferenced and so validates nothing; it is pinned by the schema digest, and the layer validator's cross-check is correctly left as an open item. Running the new record rules after v3's ownership rules keeps every v3 refusal (replay). The low-port fifth positive plus A11 is sound: positive 4 qualifies with a LABEL_BOUND server capture, and NBS on a high port is still refused.

Both stay author's readings for W03/T04. The W5 execveat statement (the script reaches the interpreter as /dev/fd/<fd>; ENOENT if the descriptor is close-on-exec) matches the reviewer's understanding of execveat(2), unverified here. One version reading is probably off: user_namespace create, 6.1 rather than 6.0 by the reviewer's recollection (N1-4).

'two roles share an entrypoint label' is unreachable (distinct schema consts, N67 is the schema refusal). The 'capabilities == []' half of the gate rule is likewise dead under the schema const, which is harmless defence in depth. V21 and C13 are the only double-defect cases. The reviewer's analysis of N01-N102 found every schema refusal a single schema error (51/51) and every model refusal schema-valid (51/51).
N98/N99 re-pin v3's binding rule that C13 no longer reaches, and N101/N102 pin the executable-map rule that v3 never pinned; they are correctly recorded as pre-existing gaps, not v4 changes.

Schema 3810 -> 4539 lines (incl. evidenceClasses), model 688 -> 1004 lines of which about 200 are check_vectors (v3 kept it in validate_native_profile_v3.py), 102 new negatives; the overrun is coverage, not new rules beyond the design.
Same pattern as I06 v2 (bare import with scripts. fallback, no __main__); the v2 -> v3 model diff is the binding lines plus the appended check_vectors.

Design §8 names slot 244's v4 as the superseded record; v5 carries v4's 45 rows unchanged and in order and the 6 packet-published rows correctly use providerCommit null with providerPacket TBD; see N1-6 for the re-derivation condition.
